headline: U.S. stocks slump into correction territory amid tech and AI worries
author: Todd C. Frankel, Shira Ovide

paragraphs.text: U.S. stock markets Friday finished their worst week since worries about President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs caused a global sell-off in April 2025, as investors grew increasingly skittish about AI and tech companies, alongside persistent concerns about inflation and interest rates.

The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid into correction territory, moving at least 10 percent below their recent closing records. The S&P 500, a broad index of major companies, was down 3.7 percent for the day, taking it down more than 7 percent for the week. The Dow was off 1.93 percent.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index erased all of its gains for 2026, dropping 5.28 percent on the day.
“It’s a meltdown right now,” said Arun Sundaram, who leads investment strategy for CFRA Research.

The stock market slide occurred despite some encouraging economic indicators this week, such as stronger-than-expected retail sales and gasoline prices that continued their ride under $4 a gallon. The national average Friday was $3.69 a gallon, according to AAA. A month ago, it was $4.28.
Investors’ fears about the future of AI appeared to drive markets, illustrated by two stocks that made ballyhooed debuts in public markets this year.
The AI company Anthropic, which started trading Thursday, was down more than 8 percent Friday. Anthropic shares closed at $88.91 a share after debuting Thursday at $83.
SpaceX — the rocket, telecommunications and AI company led by Elon Musk — saw its stock drop 7.7 percent, ending below the $135 price that SpaceX debuted with during its IPO in June.

Michael Monaghan, who oversees the Founders 100 ETF, an investment fund, said Friday that investors’ mood about AI companies has curdled in recent weeks, despite what he says is evidence of growing business interest in AI technologies.
“In my 25 years-plus investing in the markets, this is the most sentiment-driven sell-off I’ve seen,” Monaghan said.
He attributed the investor vibe shift to a confluence of events.

Big technology companies recently have signaled they planned to spend growing piles of cash building AI data centers, at the same time that the midterm elections ushered in a wave of Democratic politicians who are skeptical of AI and data centers.
Monaghan also pointed to the scandal-driven resignation of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, the leading AI computer chip company.
Shares of Nvidia were down about 14 percent Friday.
“The AI-sector’s support for the economy was called into question this week,” Oxford Economics noted in a research report.
Investors turned their attention instead to the steadier consumer-goods segment. PepsiCo’s stock jumped 1.54 percent Friday. Walmart was up 1.52 percent.
correctionA previous version of this article misstated President Donald Trump's name for his 2025 tariffs. He referred to them as “Liberation Day,” not “Independence Day.”
